attacks.claim: `.day-card` hardcodes a white background while its text uses `var(--text)`, which becomes near-white in dark mode. Light text on a white card is nearly unreadable for the ~30% of users on dark mode.

The 72px fixed action bar covers the bottom of the page on mobile, and `.planner` has no bottom padding to compensate. Sunday's tiles and their Swap and overflow controls can sit under the bar and be unreachable.
attacks.evidence: ".action-bar { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 72px; ... }" and ".planner { max-width: 960px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 16px; ... }" with Sunday as "the last child of .planner"

attacks.claim: The most frequent planner action (add a recipe's ingredients to the list, ~9.4/week, 64% on mobile) goes from one tap to six steps. The one-tap button is removed, so the redesign regresses the core task to fix a clutter goal.
attacks.evidence: "The old tile-level "+ List" button is removed to declutter tiles." and "tap the tile → recipe page → "Ingredients" tab → choose servings in the servings sheet → "Add to list" → toast with "Undo""

attacks.claim: "Generate shopping list" bulk-adds every planned recipe's ingredients for the week. The artifact specifies no undo, confirmation, or de-duplication for this path, so a tap can flood or duplicate the user's list with no recovery path.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: undo, confirmation, or de-duplication for "Generate shopping list" ("adds all planned recipes for the week"); Undo is only described for the single-recipe add.

attacks.claim: QA covers only light mode on desktop Chrome and iPhone Safari. Dark mode, which ~30% of users run, and touch drag-and-drop on mobile, which carries most traffic, are not tested, and the dark-mode defect above went unnoticed.
attacks.evidence: "Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass, pixel diffs < 1%."

attacks.claim: Lighthouse accessibility 100 was measured in light mode only. Muted dark-mode text (#a1a1a6) on the hardcoded white card would likely fail contrast, so the score does not cover the dark-mode state.

Rollout goes straight to 100% of web users with no staged percentage and no alert thresholds on the listed watch metrics. Rollback is a flag flip, which is a good safety net, but detection speed depends on someone watching the dashboards.
attacks.evidence: "Ship to 100% Tue 10:00 PT behind `planner_v7`" and "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate."

attacks.claim: No issue found under this lens; the artifact has no authn/authz or untrusted-input paths beyond the existing planner API.
"Share plan" has no described mechanism (public link, scope, expiry, or revocation), so meal-plan data could be exposed beyond the intended user.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: sharing mechanism for "Share plan" ("\"Share plan\"" appears in the action bar with no spec).

attacks.claim: No issue found under this lens; no new vendor or data-residency dependency is introduced.
attacks.evidence: "old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration)"

attacks.claim: No material issue found; a week's plan is capped at 3 recipes per day, so bulk generation is bounded.
attacks.evidence: "Each day is a `.day-card` with up to 3 recipe tiles"

attacks.claim: No issue found under this lens; no new paid calls or token spend are described.
Lazy-loaded images with explicit dimensions and a flag-based rollback are reasonable; no partial-failure handling is described for the bulk shopping-list call.
The drop behaviour when a day already has 3 tiles is unspecified, and the bulk add's handling of recipes already on the list is unclear.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: capacity rule for drag-between-days when a day has 3 tiles.

attacks.claim: The stated goal of "clearer 'this week at a glance'" has no success metric in the watch list, so the redesign cannot be judged against its own goals.
attacks.evidence: "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate."

attacks.claim: No issue found under this lens; no regulated data or platform-policy surface is described.
attacks.evidence: "Pantry is a consumer meal-planning web app."

attacks.claim: Hardcoding #ffffff in `.day-card` bypasses the colour tokens defined in `:root`, which is the root cause of the dark-mode defect and makes future theming error-prone.
No additional gate-worthy issue found beyond the lens findings above.
attacks.evidence: "Owner: growth-web · Ship: Tue 2026-11-03, 100% of web users · Epic: PAN-2207"
